proposed_targets.rationale: The existing user collection endpoint returns every row with no filtering. The human requires user-only search by name and email, so GET /api/users must support optional name and email filters while leaving /api/customers and /api/orders unchanged.
proposed_targets.evidence: Exact f629ed74d0afbcb8b5974e546c007eb5bf36663d:server.py witness: return self.reply([dict(row) for row in connection.execute(f"SELECT * FROM {table}")])

proposed_targets.rationale: The page must let users search users by name and email. The existing users section only has a heading and result container, with no search inputs, so the users section needs the requested name/email search controls; customer and order sections remain untouched.
proposed_targets.evidence:
Exact f629ed74d0afbcb8b5974e546c007eb5bf36663d:web/index.html witness:

用户列表

proposed_targets.rationale: The page query result must match the user query API. Existing client code fetches /api/users without filters, so app.js must read the name/email controls, call the same /api/users endpoint with query parameters, and render the returned user results.
proposed_targets.evidence: Exact f629ed74d0afbcb8b5974e546c007eb5bf36663d:web/app.js witness: const users = await fetch('/api/users').then(response => response.json());
